verdict.label: BUY / SELECTIVE — June Opens Green on Factory Strength, Not the Iran Deal That Didn't Sign
verdict.rationale_short: Futures point higher into the June 1 open (S&P futures 7,612.25, +0.22%) — but the weekend's base case was wrong: the Iran MoU was NOT signed. Trump called it 'largely negotiated' Saturday, yet it remains unsigned and Iran now publicly disputes the Strait of Hormuz terms, saying the waterway stays under its control. The bid is instead being driven by data: Chicago PMI jumped to 62.7, a four-year high, after a May that lifted the Nasdaq +8%. The framework holds BUY/SELECTIVE at medium because the strength is real but two of the week's confirmations are still incomplete — the 30Y sits right at 5.0% (~4.99%, not a clean Day-2 sub-5.0% confirmation), and ISM Manufacturing at 10:00 ET is unknown at the open. Act on confirmation: NVDA is in the $213-218 add zone on price ($213.35 pre-market) with a COMPUTEX keynote catalyst, but the rate confirmation is borderline — size partial, not full.

bear_case: The tape is opening green on a four-year-high Chicago PMI while quietly absorbing the fact that the weekend's central bullish binary — a signed Iran deal — failed to materialize, and Iran is now publicly contradicting Trump on who controls the Strait of Hormuz. That is a deterioration, not a confirmation: the oil market's entire ~20% May repricing assumed a signature that has not come, and a public dispute over Hormuz control is exactly the kind of crack that reverses it. The 30Y sitting at ~4.99% is being read as 'below 5.0%,' but it is one basis point of comfort, not a regime change, and ISM Manufacturing at 10:00 ET can undercut the Chicago-PMI optimism within the first trading hour. Entering June at record highs with VIX at 15.32 means the index has no defensive cushion if the Iran dispute escalates or ISM disappoints. Invalidation level: if Brent gaps above $97 on a Hormuz escalation, or SPX closes below 7,460 with the 30Y back above 5.05%, the BUY framework converts to Step Aside; a June 17 Warsh hike forces an exit of all longs regardless of level.
